    Check the status of Fireflies.ai API credentials for the current user.
    
    Re-verifies the stored API key against Fireflies — a key revoked on the
    Fireflies side will be reported as Invalid here even if it is still
    present in the local store.
    
    Returns:
        A human-readable credential status block (no secrets).
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=auth

  delete_fireflies_credentials
    Delete the current user's Fireflies.ai API credentials.
    
    After deletion, you'll need to call `set_fireflies_credentials` again with
    a valid API key before any Fireflies tool will succeed.
    
    Returns:
        Success or error message.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=auth

  list_fireflies_transcripts
    List or search meeting transcripts from Fireflies.ai.
    
    Use this to find meetings — by keyword, date range, organizer / participant
    email(s), Fireflies user id, or channel. Returns lightweight metadata
    (no sentences, no summary) so the result fits comfortably in context.
    Call ``get_fireflies_transcript(id=...)`` afterwards to drill into one
    meeting.
    
    Args:
        keyword: Free-text search; ``scope`` controls whether it matches title
            only (default), sentences (spoken content), or both.
        scope: One of "title", "sentences", "all". When ``scope`` is provided,
            ``keyword`` becomes required by Fireflies.
        from_date: ISO 8601 lower bound, e.g. ``"2024-07-08T00:00:00.000Z"``.
        to_date: ISO 8601 upper bound (same format).
        host_email: Filter by host email.
        organizers: List of organizer emails (preferred for organizer filtering).
        participants: List of participant emails (preferred for participant
            filtering).
        organizer_email: Single-organizer filter, kept for backward
            compatibility. Cannot be combined with ``organizers`` /
            ``participants``.
        participant_email: Single-participant filter, kept for backward
            compatibility. Cannot be combined with ``organizers`` /
            ``participants``.
        user_id: Filter meetings where this Fireflies user id was the organizer
            or a participant.
        channel_id: Filter meetings that belong to a Fireflies channel.
        mine: When True, only return transcripts owned by the API key's user.
        limit: Max results to return (Fireflies caps this at 50; default 25).
        skip: Pagination offset (default 0).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with the matching transcripts. Each entry includes id, title,
        date, duration, attendees, speakers, transcript_url, and a
        ``meeting_info`` block (``fred_joined`` / ``silent_meeting`` /
        ``summary_status``) that signals whether the bot actually joined and
        whether the AI summary has finished processing.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=transcripts
      - keyword (string)
      - scope (string)
      - from_date (string)
      - to_date (string)
      - host_email (string)
      - participant_email (string)
      - organizer_email (string)
      - organizers (string[])
      - participants (string[])
      - user_id (string)
      - channel_id (string)
      - mine (boolean)
      - limit (integer)
      - skip (integer)

  get_fireflies_transcript
    Fetch the full content of a single Fireflies meeting transcript.
    
    Returns metadata + summary (overview, action items, keywords, topics) +
    speakers + the full sentence-by-sentence transcript. Long meetings
    produce large responses; call ``list_fireflies_transcripts`` first when
    the user only needs to identify a meeting.
    
    Args:
        id: Transcript id (from ``list_fireflies_transcripts``).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with the full transcript payload.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=transcripts
      - id (string) (required)

  get_fireflies_user_info
    Fetch the connected Fireflies account's profile and usage signals.
    
    Useful before quota-sensitive operations: ``minutes_consumed`` and
    ``num_transcripts`` give a coarse read on how close the account is to
    its plan limits, and ``is_admin`` / ``integrations`` reveal what the
    key can do (e.g. team-scoped queries or which calendar/CRM is linked).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with the current user's id, email, name, transcript count,
        consumed minutes, recent meeting / transcript ids, admin flag, and
        the list of connected integrations. Fields the account does not
        expose (e.g. some signals on Free plans) are omitted.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=user

  add_fireflies_to_live_meeting
    Invite the Fireflies.ai notetaker (Fred) to an in-progress meeting.
    
    SIDE EFFECT: this actually joins a real meeting — confirm the user wants
    to proceed before chaining it to other tools. Rate limit: 3 requests per
    20 minutes (a tight, separate bucket from the daily quota).
    
    Args:
        meeting_link: HTTPS URL for the live meeting (Zoom / Google Meet / Teams /
            Webex). Must be the exact join link.
        title: Optional title for the resulting transcript (max 256 chars).
        duration: How long Fred should stay (minutes). Min 15, max 120,
            default 60 if omitted.
        language: Language code (e.g. "en", "es", "de"). Max 5 characters.
            Defaults to English. See Fireflies' Language Codes page for the
            full list.
        meeting_password: Password if the meeting requires one (max 32 chars).
        attendees: Optional list of expected meeting participants. Each item is
            a dict with optional ``displayName`` / ``email`` / ``phoneNumber``
            fields, e.g. ``[{"email": "alice@x.com", "displayName": "Alice"}]``.
            Helps Fred match transcript speakers to known people.
    
    Returns:
        JSON with ``success: true`` if Fred was dispatched.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=meetings
      - meeting_link (string) (required)
      - title (string)
      - duration (integer)
      - language (string)
      - meeting_password (string)
      - attendees (object[])

  list_fireflies_channels
    List the Fireflies meeting channels (folders) visible to the connected
    account.
    
    Use this before calling ``list_fireflies_transcripts(channel_id=...)`` —
    that filter needs a Fireflies channel id which is not visible elsewhere.
    
    Returns:
        JSON with each channel's ``id``, ``title``, ``is_private``,
        ``created_at`` / ``updated_at``, and ``created_by``.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=channels

  list_fireflies_users
    List the Fireflies users visible to the connected account.
    
    Use this before calling ``list_fireflies_transcripts`` with ``user_id`` /
    ``organizers`` / ``participants`` filters — those filters need Fireflies
    user ids or emails which this tool surfaces.
    
    Note: on personal plans this typically returns only the connected user.
    Full team listings require admin-level credentials on a paid plan.
    
    Returns:
        JSON with each user's ``user_id``, ``email``, ``name``,
        ``num_transcripts``, ``is_admin``, ``is_calendar_in_sync`` and
        connected ``integrations``.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=users

  get_fireflies_active_meetings
    List meetings that are currently in progress for the connected account.
    
    Useful before calling ``add_fireflies_to_live_meeting`` to avoid inviting
    Fred to a meeting he is already in, or to check which meetings Fred is

    Args:

            Defaults to the connected account.

        ``privacy``, and ``state``.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=meetings
      - email (string)
      - states (string[])

  list_fireflies_soundbites
    List Fireflies soundbites (short highlight clips cut from meetings).
    
    Fireflies requires exactly one scope — at least one of ``mine`` /

        ``preview`` URLs, ``user`` (creator), and ``created_from`` (source
        meeting). Call ``get_fireflies_soundbite(id=...)`` for full detail.
    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=soundbites
      - mine (boolean)
      - my_team (boolean)
      - transcript_id (string)
      - limit (integer)
      - skip (integer)

  get_fireflies_soundbite

        ``start_time`` / ``end_time``, ``media_type``, ``created_at``,

    meta: toolkit=fireflies, toolkit_service=soundbites
      - id (string) (required)

  start_microsoft365_auth
    Start Microsoft 365 OAuth 2.0 authorization.
    
    When to call:
      Use this tool whenever the user asks to "connect Microsoft 365",
      "connect Outlook", "authorize Microsoft 365 mail", or any other
      Microsoft 365-related capability and there is no existing valid
      credential. Do NOT call it just to double-check existing connections —
      other tools will trigger the auth flow automatically when needed.
    
    What it does:
      Builds the Microsoft Identity Platform v2.0 authorization URL for the
      current ``accio_id`` (multi-tenant isolation) and returns it inside a
      human-friendly instruction message. The URL is what the end user must
      open in their browser to grant the requested scopes
      (``offline_access``, ``User.Read``, ``Mail.ReadWrite``,
      ``Calendars.ReadWrite``, ``Files.ReadWrite.All``,
      ``Chat.ReadWrite``, ``Notes.ReadWrite.All``, etc.).
    
    Args:
      user_email: Optional Microsoft account email. When provided it is sent
        as ``login_hint`` so Microsoft prefills the account picker. Leaving
        it empty lets the user pick any account they have access to.
    
    Returns:
      A Markdown-formatted instruction message. The relevant fields are:
        - ``authUrl``: the authorization URL string
        - guidance text in the user's locale (zh/en)
      No credential is persisted at this stage; persistence happens in the
      ``GET /microsoft365/callback`` route after the browser completes the flow.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=auth
      - user_email (string)

  set_microsoft365_credentials
    Manually register a Microsoft Graph access token.
    
    When to call:
      Use this tool only when the user has obtained a Microsoft Graph access
      token outside the in-app OAuth flow (e.g. from Azure Postman, a
      pre-existing service principal token exchange, or another integration)
      and wants the MCP server to use it directly. For first-time end-user
      authorization, prefer ``start_microsoft365_auth`` instead.
    
    Validation:
      The token is verified by calling ``GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me``
      BEFORE persistence. If the call fails (network error, 401, missing
      ``mail`` / ``userPrincipalName``), nothing is written to the credential
      store and the function returns a human-readable error message.
    
    Storage:
      On success the credential is stored under the current ``accio_id`` and
      keyed by the email returned from ``/me``. Multiple Microsoft 365 accounts
      under the same workspace are kept independent.
    
    Args:
      access_token: A non-empty Microsoft Graph delegated access token.
      refresh_token: Optional refresh token. Without it, the credential cannot
        be auto-refreshed and tools may need to re-prompt the user when the
        access token expires.
      expires_in_seconds: Optional remaining lifetime of the access token, in
        seconds. When provided, future requests will refresh the token a few
        minutes before this deadline.
      scope: Optional space-separated list of granted scopes (e.g.
        ``"User.Read Mail.ReadWrite"``). Used to drive future refresh calls
        when set.
    
    Returns:
      Markdown text. On success the message contains the literal word
      ``connected`` and shows the email of the connected account. On failure
      the message starts with ``Error:`` and includes the underlying reason.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=auth
      - access_token (string) (required)
      - refresh_token (string)
      - expires_in_seconds (integer)
      - scope (string)

  search_microsoft365_emails
    Search messages in the authenticated user's Microsoft 365 mailbox.
    
    When to call:
      Use this tool whenever the user wants to LIST or FIND emails —
      e.g. "show my unread mail from Bob this week", "find the invoice from
      Stripe", "what's in my Sent Items?". Prefer this over
      ``get_microsoft365_email_detail`` when the message id is unknown.
    
    Authentication:
      Requires a previously connected Microsoft 365 account with the
      ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope. If the credential is missing or revoked, the
      tool returns an actionable error string asking the user to call
      ``start_microsoft365_auth`` (no exception is raised to the Agent).
    
    Args:
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email address of the
        authenticated user (e.g. ``"alice@contoso.com"``). When omitted /
        empty string, the tool auto-locates the credential as long as the
        current accio has **exactly one** connected Microsoft 365 account.
      query: OPTIONAL Microsoft Graph ``$search`` expression (KQL-style).
        Examples:
          - ``"from:bob@contoso.com"``
          - ``"subject:invoice received:>=2024-01-01"``
          - ``"hasAttachment:true"``
        Empty string → list recent messages in ``folder``.
      folder: OPTIONAL well-known folder name. Default ``"inbox"``. Other
        common values: ``"sentitems"``, ``"drafts"``, ``"deleteditems"``,
        ``"archive"``. Pass an empty string to search across all folders.
      top: OPTIONAL page size (1-999). Default ``20``.
      next_link: OPTIONAL pagination URL returned by a previous call as
        ``nextLink``. When provided, all other paging params are ignored.
    
    Returns:
      On success — a Markdown text containing:
        * a one-line count summary
        * a numbered list of messages (subject / from / id)
        * a fenced ```json``` block with the messages array and optional nextLink
    
      On failure — a single-line failure reason followed by an action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=mail
      - user_email (string)
      - query (string)
      - folder (string)
      - top (integer)
      - next_link (string)

  get_microsoft365_email_detail
    Fetch a single message by id, including full body and recipients.
    
    When to call:
      Call this AFTER ``search_microsoft365_emails`` returns a message id and
      the user wants to read the full content / quote it / reply to it.
    
    Authentication:
      Requires the ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.
    
    Args:
      message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id (the ``id`` field returned
        by ``search_microsoft365_emails``).
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Same semantic as in ``search_microsoft365_emails``.
      body_format: OPTIONAL. ``"text"`` (default) or ``"html"``.
    
    Returns:
      On success — Markdown text with key headers plus a fenced json block.
      On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=mail
      - message_id (string) (required)
      - user_email (string)
      - body_format (string)

  send_microsoft365_email
    Send a new email on behalf of the authenticated Microsoft 365 user.
    
    When to call:
      Use this whenever the user asks to "send an email", "reply via Outlook",
      "email Bob the report", etc. This sends immediately — there is no
      draft tool yet.
    
    Authentication:
      Requires ``Mail.Send`` scope for the ``/me/sendMail`` endpoint of

      subject: REQUIRED. Subject line.
      body: REQUIRED. Mail body content.
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox that will appear as sender.
      cc: OPTIONAL list of CC addresses.
      bcc: OPTIONAL list of BCC addresses.
      body_format: OPTIONAL ``"text"`` (default) or ``"html"``.
      save_to_sent_items: OPTIONAL bool, default ``True``.
    
    Returns:
      On success — a one-line confirmation + fenced json block.
      On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=mail
      - to (string[]) (required)
      - subject (string) (required)
      - body (string) (required)
      - user_email (string)
      - cc (string[])
      - bcc (string[])
      - body_format (string)
      - save_to_sent_items (boolean)

  download_microsoft365_attachment
    Download the content of an email attachment.
    
    When to call:
      Use this after ``list_microsoft365_email_attachments`` returns an
      attachment id and the user wants to retrieve the actual file content.
    
    Behavior:
      - **Text-based attachments** (txt, csv, json, xml, html, md, yaml, log,
        etc.) are base64-decoded and the plain text content is returned directly
        so you can display it, process it, or write it to a file.
      - **Binary attachments** (pdf, docx, xlsx, images, zip, etc.) are returned
        as raw base64 content. You should write this base64 string to a local
        file using the appropriate tool (e.g. create a file with decoded bytes).
    
    Authentication:
      Requires ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.
    
    Args:
      message_id: REQUIRED. The Graph message id containing the attachment.
      attachment_id: REQUIRED. The Graph attachment id to download.
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Authenticated mailbox.
    
    Returns:
      On success — attachment metadata + actual content (decoded text or base64).
      On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=mail
      - message_id (string) (required)
      - attachment_id (string) (required)
      - user_email (string)

  list_microsoft365_mail_folders
    List all mail folders in the user's mailbox.
    
    When to call:
      Use this when the user asks "what folders do I have?", "show my mail
      folders", or when you need a folder id for ``move_microsoft365_message``
      or ``copy_microsoft365_message`` and the target is a custom folder
      (not a well-known name like archive/inbox/drafts).
    
    Authentication:
      Requires ``Mail.Read`` or ``Mail.ReadWrite`` scope.
    
    Args:
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
      include_children: OPTIONAL. If True, also fetches child folders
        (one level deep). Default False.

  get_microsoft365_user_profile
    Return the connected Microsoft 365 user's profile (verifies credential).
    
    When to call:
      Two main scenarios:
        1) After ``start_microsoft365_auth`` / ``set_microsoft365_credentials``
           — to confirm the credential actually works against Microsoft Graph.
        2) Before a multi-step workflow when you want a cheap pre-flight check
           (this hits ``GET /me``, the lightest Graph endpoint that requires
           ``User.Read``).
      Do NOT call it on every mail/contacts request — those tools already
      perform their own auth check.
    
    Authentication:
      Requires ``User.Read`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.
    
    Args:
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email of the authenticated user.
        When omitted, the tool auto-locates the credential if exactly one
        account is connected.
    
    Returns:
      On success — Markdown text starting with ``✅ Microsoft 365 profile verified``
      followed by a fenced json block.
      On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=profile
      - user_email (string)

  get_microsoft365_drive_item

  upload_microsoft365_drive_file
    Upload a file (up to 250 MB) to OneDrive.
    
    When to call:
      Use when the user asks to "save this to OneDrive", "upload a file",
      "put this document in my drive", etc. Supports both text and binary
      files.
    
    Behavior:
      - **Text files** (default): pass the file content directly as a string
        in ``content`` with ``content_encoding="text"``.
      - **Binary files** (images, PDF, docx, etc.): pass base64-encoded file
        content in ``content`` with ``content_encoding="base64"``. The tool
        will decode it before uploading.
    
    Args:
      file_name: REQUIRED. Target file name (e.g. "report.pdf", "photo.png").
      content: REQUIRED. File content — plain text string when
        content_encoding="text", or base64-encoded string when
        content_encoding="base64".
      user_email: OPTIONAL.
      parent_path: OPTIONAL. Parent folder path (e.g. "/Documents").
        Empty = root.
      content_type: OPTIONAL. MIME type (e.g. "application/pdf",
        "image/png"). If empty, auto-detected from file extension.
      content_encoding: OPTIONAL. How ``content`` is encoded:
        - ``"text"`` (default) — content is plain text, uploaded as-is.
        - ``"base64"`` — content is base64-encoded binary, decoded before upload.
    
    Returns:
      Confirmation text + created item metadata json.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=drive
      - file_name (string) (required)
      - content (string) (required)
      - user_email (string)
      - parent_path (string)
      - content_type (string)
      - content_encoding (string)

  download_microsoft365_drive_file
    Download and return the actual content of a file from OneDrive.
    
    When to call:
      Use this whenever the user wants to download, read, view, open, or get
      the content of a file from OneDrive. This is the ONLY tool that returns
      actual file content.
    
      Typical workflow:
        1. ``search_microsoft365_drive`` or ``list_microsoft365_drive_items``
           → find the file (get item_id)
        2. ``download_microsoft365_drive_file`` (this tool) → get file content
    
      Do NOT use ``get_microsoft365_drive_item`` for downloading — that tool
      only returns metadata, not content.
    
    Behavior:
      - **Text-based files** (txt, csv, json, xml, html, md, yaml, py, etc.)
        are returned as decoded plain text, ready to display or write locally.
      - **Binary files** (pdf, docx, xlsx, images, zip, etc.) are returned as
        base64-encoded content. You should decode and write to a local file.
    
    Authentication:
      Requires ``Files.ReadWrite`` scope on the connected Microsoft 365 account.
    
    Args:
      item_id: The Graph driveItem id. One of item_id or path is required.
      path: Path relative to root (e.g. "/Documents/report.xlsx").
      user_email: OPTIONAL. Microsoft 365 email.
    
    Returns:
      On success — file metadata + actual content (decoded text or base64).
      On failure — single-line failure reason + action hint.
    meta: toolkit=microsoft365, toolkit_service=drive
      - item_id (string)
      - path (string)
      - user_email (string)

  setup_gmail_watch
    Set up Gmail watch for push notifications.
    
    Registers the user's mailbox with Gmail push (Pub/Sub). When new mail matches
    the optional filter_query, a MetaQ event is sent for downstream consumers.
    Watch expires in about 7 days; use renew_gmail_watch to extend.
    
    Args:
        user_google_email: User's Gmail address (must be authenticated).
        pubsub_topic_name: Full Pub/Sub topic, e.g. projects/my-project/topics/my-topic.
            Defaults to projects/accio-oauth/topics/gmail-notifications.
        label_ids: Label IDs to watch (e.g. ["INBOX"]). If omitted, all labels are watched.
        filter_query: Optional Gmail search-style filter (e.g. from:boss@company.com subject:urgent).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with watch status, historyId, and expiration (ms).
    meta: toolkit=google, toolkit_service=gmail
      - user_google_email (string) (required)
      - pubsub_topic_name (string)
      - label_ids (string[])
      - filter_query (string)

  stop_gmail_watch

  create_github_repo
    Create a new GitHub repository, either under the authenticated user
    or under a GitHub organization.
    
    Call this tool when the user asks:
    - "Create a new repo called my-project"
    - "Help me set up a new private GitHub repository"
    - "Initialize a new project on GitHub"
    - "Create a repo named foo under the my-org organization"
    
    Args:
        name: Repository name (required). Must be unique under the chosen
              owner (user or org). Example: "my-awesome-project".
        description: Short description of the repository.
        private: If True, create a private repo. Default False (public).
        auto_init: If True, initialize with a README. Default True.
        org: If provided, create the repo under this GitHub organization
             instead of the authenticated user's account. The authenticated
             user must have permission to create repositories in that org
             (org "Repository creation" policy + sufficient role). When
             omitted (default), the repo is created under the user's
             account — backward compatible.
        user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    
    Returns:
        On success — JSON with the created repo: full_name, html_url, private,
        description, default_branch, created_at.
    
        On failure — single-line error with action suggestion. Common org
        failures: 403 (insufficient permission / org policy forbids creation),
        404 (org not found or not visible to the token), 422 (name already
        taken in the org).
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - name (string) (required)
      - description (string)
      - private (boolean)
      - auto_init (boolean)
      - org (string)
      - user_login (string)

  fork_github_repo

    Call this tool when the user asks:

    Args:
        owner: Owner of the repository to fork, e.g. "facebook".
        repo: Repository name to fork, e.g. "react".
        organization: If provided, fork to this org instead of the user's account.
                      The user must be a member of the org.
        name: Custom name for the forked repo. Default is the original repo name.
        user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    
    Returns:
        On success — JSON with the forked repo: full_name, html_url, private,
        description, parent (source repo full_name).
    
        On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - organization (string)
      - name (string)
      - user_login (string)

  list_github_repos
    List GitHub repositories accessible to the authenticated user,
    including **private repos** that are invisible without login.
    
    By default, lists repos owned by / accessible to the authenticated user
    (``GET /user/repos``). When ``organization`` is supplied, the tool
    switches to listing repos under that organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``);
    private repos the authenticated user has access to within the org are
    included.
    
    Note: this tool intentionally does NOT accept a ``username`` filter.
    GitHub's ``GET /users/{username}/repos`` endpoint only ever returns
    public repositories — even when authenticated and even when the
    username matches the caller — so exposing it here would mislead users
    into thinking private repos can be listed by username. To see your
    own private repos, simply omit ``organization``.
    
    Call this tool when the user asks:
    - "What repos do I have?"
    - "Show me my private repositories"
    - "List my recently updated projects"
    - "Show all repositories under the alibaba organization"
    
    Args:
        user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
        visibility: Filter — "all" (default), "public", or "private".
            Only applies when listing the authenticated user's own repos
            (i.e. ``organization`` is not provided).
        sort: Sort field — "created", "updated" (default), "pushed", or "full_name".
        per_page: Results per page, 1–100. Default 20.
        page: Page number starting at 1.
        organization: If provided, list repositories under this GitHub
            organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``).
    
    Returns:
        On success — JSON ``{ repos: [...], pagination: {...}, user_login,
        scope: {...} }``. ``scope`` describes which listing was performed:
        ``{"type": "self" | "org", "target": <name or null>}``.
        Each repo: full_name, description, html_url, private, language,
        stargazers_count, forks_count, updated_at, default_branch.
    
        On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - user_login (string)
      - visibility (string)
      - sort (string)
      - per_page (integer)
      - page (integer)
      - organization (string)

  list_github_issues
    List GitHub issues (search-backed; cross-repo or scoped).
    
    `filter` is **scope-aware** when omitted: with `owner`/`repo`/`org` it
    defaults to `"none"` (all items in that scope); without scope it defaults
    to `"assigned"` (the user's personal dashboard). For when-to-use guidance,
    user-wording → `filter` mapping, and pagination caveats, see SKILL.md
    `github-tools` (Pitfalls 3, 4, 6).
    
    Args:
        filter: One of `"assigned"` / `"authored"` / `"mentioned"` / `"none"`.
            Leave unset for the scope-aware default. `"none"` requires
            `owner`/`repo`/`org`.
        state: `"open"` (default) / `"closed"` / `"all"`. Case-insensitive.
        owner: Repo owner OR user/org login. With `repo` → single repo;
            alone → `user:owner` (all repos of that owner).
        repo: Repo name; requires `owner`.
        org: Limit to repos owned by this org (`org:` qualifier).
        labels: Comma-separated labels, e.g. `"bug,help wanted"`.
        sort: `"created"` / `"updated"` (default) / `"comments"`. Descending only.
        per_page: 1–100, default 20.
        page: 1-based. GitHub caps search at 1000 results total.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON `{ issues: [...], pagination: {page, per_page, returned,
        total_count, incomplete_results}, query, user_login }`. Each issue:
        number, title, state, user, assignees, html_url, comments, labels,
        created_at, updated_at. `assignees` is a list of login strings (empty
        when no one is assigned).
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - filter (string)
      - state (string)
      - owner (string)
      - repo (string)
      - org (string)
      - labels (string)
      - sort (string)
      - per_page (integer)
      - page (integer)
      - user_login (string)

  list_github_pull_requests
    List GitHub pull requests (search-backed; cross-repo or scoped).
    
    `filter` is **scope-aware** when omitted: with `owner`/`repo`/`org` it
    defaults to `"none"` (all items in that scope); without scope it defaults
    to `"review_requested"` (PRs awaiting the user's review). Branch filtering
    (`head` / `base`) is not exposed. For when-to-use guidance, user-wording
    → `filter` mapping, and pagination caveats, see SKILL.md `github-tools`
    (Pitfalls 3, 4, 6).
    
    Args:
        filter: One of `"review_requested"` / `"reviewed_by"` / `"authored"`
            / `"assigned"` / `"mentioned"` / `"none"`. Leave unset for the
            scope-aware default. `"none"` requires `owner`/`repo`/`org`.
        state: `"open"` (default) / `"closed"` / `"all"`. Case-insensitive.
        owner / repo / org / labels: Same semantics as `list_github_issues`.
        sort: `"created"` / `"updated"` (default) / `"comments"`. Descending only.
        per_page: 1–100, default 20.
        page: 1-based. GitHub caps search at 1000 results total.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON `{ pull_requests: [...], pagination: {page, per_page,
        returned, total_count, incomplete_results}, query, user_login }`.
        Each PR: number, title, state, draft, user, assignees, html_url,
        head, base, created_at, updated_at. `assignees` is a list of login
        strings (empty when no one is assigned). For requested reviewers,
        use `get_github_pull_request_content`. (`head`/`base` may be null
        on search results.)
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - filter (string)
      - state (string)
      - owner (string)
      - repo (string)
      - org (string)
      - labels (string)
      - sort (string)
      - per_page (integer)
      - page (integer)
      - user_login (string)

  get_github_issue_content
    Drill into a single GitHub issue: body + metadata + first page of
    comments. Pair with `list_github_issues` to discover `number`.
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner, e.g. `"facebook"`.
        repo: Repo name, e.g. `"react"`.
        number: Issue number (the integer after `#`).
        include_comments: If True (default), also fetch the first page of
            conversation comments. Set False to save one API call when only
            the body is needed.
        comments_per_page: 1–100, default 30. Only the first page is fetched;
            inspect `pagination.has_more` and re-issue with paging if needed.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON `{ issue: {...}, comments: [...] | null, pagination:
        {comments_returned, comments_per_page, has_more}, user_login }`.
    
        Issue fields: number, title, state, state_reason, user, html_url,
        comments (count), labels, assignees, milestone, body, created_at,
        updated_at, closed_at.
        Comment: id, user, html_url, body, created_at, updated_at.
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - number (integer) (required)
      - include_comments (boolean)
      - comments_per_page (integer)
      - user_login (string)

  get_github_pull_request_content
    Drill into a single GitHub PR: body + merge state + diff stats + first
    page of conversation comments + first page of line-level review comments.
    Pair with `list_github_pull_requests` to discover `number`.
    
    Note: returns diff *stats* (`additions`/`deletions`/`changed_files`), not
    the file-by-file patch. For the patch, point the user at `html_url + ".diff"`.
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner, e.g. `"facebook"`.
        repo: Repo name, e.g. `"react"`.
        number: PR number (the integer after `#`).
        include_comments: If True (default), fetch the first page of
            conversation comments (PR timeline).
        include_review_comments: If True (default), fetch the first page of
            line-level review comments anchored to the diff.
        comments_per_page: 1–100, default 30. Applies to both comment kinds;
            only one page is fetched per kind. `pagination.*_has_more` tells
            you whether to follow up.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON `{ pull_request: {...}, comments: [...] | null,
        review_comments: [...] | null, pagination: {comments_returned,
        review_comments_returned, comments_per_page, comments_has_more,
        review_comments_has_more}, user_login }`.
    
        PR fields: number, title, state, draft, user, html_url, head, base,
        labels, assignees, requested_reviewers, milestone, body, merged,
        mergeable, mergeable_state, merge_commit_sha, commits, additions,
        deletions, changed_files, review_comments (count), comments (count),
        created_at, updated_at, closed_at, merged_at.
        Comment: id, user, html_url, body, created_at, updated_at.
        Review comment additionally: path, line, side, start_line, start_side,
        commit_id, in_reply_to_id.
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - number (integer) (required)
      - include_comments (boolean)
      - include_review_comments (boolean)
      - comments_per_page (integer)
      - user_login (string)

  create_github_issue
    Create a new GitHub issue in the given repository.
    
    Use this for the **initial creation** only. To later edit, close, comment,
    or change labels/assignees, call ``update_github_issue``.
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner login (user or org).
        repo: Repo name.
        title: Issue title (required, non-empty).
        body: Markdown body of the issue. Optional.
        labels: Comma-separated label names already defined in the repo,
            e.g. ``"bug,help wanted"``. Unknown labels will be silently
            ignored by GitHub.
        assignees: Comma-separated GitHub logins. The caller must have push
            access to the repo, and assignees themselves must be repo
            collaborators — GitHub silently drops invalid assignees.
        milestone: Numeric milestone id (not the title). Optional.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON of the new issue projected via ``_slim_issue_full``
        (number, title, state, body, labels, assignees, html_url, ...).
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - title (string) (required)
      - body (string)
      - labels (string)
      - assignees (string)
      - milestone (integer)
      - user_login (string)

  update_github_issue
    Apply a single mutation to an existing issue, dispatched by ``action``.
    
    This tool intentionally aggregates 6 issue write endpoints under one tool
    so the LLM picks an *intent* (close, comment, ...) instead of one of N
    similarly-named tools. Each ``action`` consumes a specific subset of the
    optional parameters; unrelated parameters are ignored.
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner.
        repo: Repo name.
        number: Issue number.
        action: One of:
            - ``"edit"`` — uses ``title`` and/or ``body``. At least one required.
            - ``"close"`` — closes the issue. Optional ``state_reason``:
              ``"completed"`` (default) or ``"not_planned"``.
            - ``"reopen"`` — reopens the issue. No other params.
            - ``"comment"`` — adds a conversation comment. Requires
              ``comment_body``.
            - ``"set_labels"`` — **replaces the full label set**. ``labels``
              is a comma-separated list (empty string ``""`` clears all labels).
            - ``"set_assignees"`` — **replaces the full assignee set** by
              diffing against the current state. ``assignees`` is a
              comma-separated list of GitHub logins (empty string clears).
        title: For ``action="edit"``.
        body: For ``action="edit"``.
        state_reason: For ``action="close"``.
        comment_body: For ``action="comment"``.
        labels: For ``action="set_labels"``.
        assignees: For ``action="set_assignees"``.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the projected issue
        (or comment, for ``action="comment"``).
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - number (integer) (required)
      - action (string) (required)
      - title (string)
      - body (string)
      - state_reason (string)
      - comment_body (string)
      - labels (string)
      - assignees (string)
      - user_login (string)

  create_github_pull_request
    Open a new pull request.
    
    Use this for the **initial creation** only. To later edit, close, comment,
    add reviewers, or change labels/assignees, call ``update_github_pull_request``.
    To approve / request changes / merge, call ``review_github_pull_request``.
    
    Args:
        owner: Target repo owner.
        repo: Target repo name.
        title: PR title (required, non-empty).
        head: Source branch. For same-repo PRs use ``"feature-branch"``;
            for cross-fork PRs use ``"fork-owner:feature-branch"``.
        base: Target branch in the destination repo, e.g. ``"main"``.
        body: Markdown body. Optional.
        draft: Open as a draft PR. Defaults to ``False``.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON of the new PR projected via ``_slim_pull_request_full``.
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - title (string) (required)
      - head (string) (required)
      - base (string) (required)
      - body (string)
      - draft (boolean)
      - user_login (string)

  update_github_pull_request
    Apply a single mutation to an existing pull request, dispatched by ``action``.
    
    Mirrors ``update_github_issue`` plus a ``"set_reviewers"`` action.
    Approve / request changes / merge are intentionally **not** here —
    use ``review_github_pull_request`` for those (they are review events,
    not property edits, and merge is destructive).
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner.
        repo: Repo name.
        number: PR number.
        action: One of:
            - ``"edit"`` — uses ``title`` / ``body`` / ``base``. At least one required.
              ``base`` retargets the PR to a different branch.
            - ``"close"`` — closes the PR without merging. No other params.
            - ``"reopen"`` — reopens a closed PR. No other params.
            - ``"comment"`` — adds a conversation comment via the issues
              endpoint. Requires ``comment_body``.
            - ``"set_labels"`` — replaces the full label set. ``labels`` is
              comma-separated; empty string clears.
            - ``"set_assignees"`` — replaces the full assignee set
              (diff-and-apply). ``assignees`` comma-separated; empty clears.
            - ``"set_reviewers"`` — replaces requested reviewers
              (diff-and-apply). At least one of ``reviewers`` or
              ``team_reviewers`` must be provided; pass ``""`` for an
              already-supplied field to clear that side.
        title: For ``action="edit"``.
        body: For ``action="edit"``.
        base: For ``action="edit"``.
        comment_body: For ``action="comment"``.
        labels: For ``action="set_labels"``.
        assignees: For ``action="set_assignees"``.
        reviewers: For ``action="set_reviewers"``. Comma-separated user logins.
        team_reviewers: For ``action="set_reviewers"``. Comma-separated team
            slugs (org-only).
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the projected PR
        (or comment, for ``action="comment"``).
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - number (integer) (required)
      - action (string) (required)
      - title (string)
      - body (string)
      - base (string)
      - comment_body (string)
      - labels (string)
      - assignees (string)
      - reviewers (string)
      - team_reviewers (string)
      - user_login (string)

  review_github_pull_request
    Submit a review event or merge a pull request.
    
    These actions are kept apart from ``update_github_pull_request`` because
    they are not property edits — a review is an immutable event in the PR
    timeline, and a merge is destructive (cannot be undone via the API).
    
    Args:
        owner: Repo owner.
        repo: Repo name.
        number: PR number.
        action: One of:
            - ``"approve"`` — submit an approving review. ``body`` optional.
            - ``"request_changes"`` — submit a changes-requested review.
              ``body`` is **required** by GitHub and validated here.
            - ``"comment"`` — submit a non-blocking review comment. ``body``
              is **required** when there are no ``line_comments``.
            - ``"merge"`` — merge the PR. Uses ``merge_method`` /
              ``commit_title`` / ``commit_message`` / ``sha``.
        body: Review body markdown. Semantics depend on ``action``; see above.
        line_comments: Optional line-level comments for the review, each
            shaped ``{"path": ..., "line": ..., "side": "RIGHT"|"LEFT",
            "body": ...}``. Only applies to review actions, not ``"merge"``.
        commit_id: Optional SHA the review should anchor to. Defaults to PR head.
        merge_method: For ``action="merge"``: ``"merge"`` (default) /
            ``"squash"`` / ``"rebase"``.
        commit_title: For ``action="merge"``. Optional.
        commit_message: For ``action="merge"``. Optional.
        sha: For ``action="merge"``. If set, GitHub rejects the merge unless
            the PR head still matches this SHA — defends against merging a
            stale branch.
        user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.
    
    Returns:
        Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the relevant payload
        (review object for review actions, merge result for merge).
    
        Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.
    meta: toolkit=github, toolkit_service=repos
      - owner (string) (required)
      - repo (string) (required)
      - number (integer) (required)
      - action (string) (required)
      - body (string)
      - line_comments (object[])
      - commit_id (string)
      - merge_method (string)
      - commit_title (string)
      - commit_message (string)
      - sha (string)
      - user_login (string)

  get_linkedin_user_info
    Fetch the LinkedIn OpenID Connect user profile of the currently authorized account.
    
    WHEN TO CALL:
    - The user asks about their LinkedIn account info / profile / email;
    - You need to verify whether LinkedIn authorization is still valid before
      performing a write action such as sharing a post;
    - You need the user's Person URN (`urn:li:person:{sub}`) to compose other
      LinkedIn API requests.
    
    REQUIRED OAUTH SCOPES: `openid`, `profile`, `email`.
    
    Args:
        linkedin_user_id: Optional. LinkedIn user id (the `sub` returned by
            `/v2/userinfo`). Only needed when multiple LinkedIn accounts are
            bound to the same accio_id. When omitted, the single bound account
            is used automatically.
    
    Returns:
        On success — a human-readable summary followed by a JSON payload with
        keys: `sub`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `picture`, `locale`,
        `email`, `email_verified`.
        On failure — a single-line reason plus an action suggestion (e.g.
        re-authorize via `start_linkedin_auth`). No raw stack trace is exposed.
    
    Example:
        get_linkedin_user_info()
        get_linkedin_user_info(linkedin_user_id="abc123XYZ")
    meta: toolkit=linkedin, toolkit_service=consumer
      - linkedin_user_id (string)

  share_text_on_linkedin
    Publish a plain-text post to the currently authorized LinkedIn account.
    
    WHEN TO CALL:
    - The user asks to "post a status / tweet / update / dynamic" on LinkedIn;
    - The user wants to publish a pure-text announcement or thought without
      any link or image attachment.
    - If the user also provides a URL to share, prefer `share_article_on_linkedin`
      instead.
    
    REQUIRED OAUTH SCOPE: `w_member_social`.
    
    Args:
        text: Required. The plain-text content to publish. LinkedIn will
            render line breaks as-is. Mandatory and must be non-empty.
        visibility: Optional. Post visibility. Allowed: `"PUBLIC"` (default,
            visible to everyone) or `"CONNECTIONS"` (visible to 1st-degree
            connections only). Any other value falls back to `"PUBLIC"`.
        linkedin_user_id: Optional. Same semantics as in
            `get_linkedin_user_info`. Needed only when multiple LinkedIn
            accounts are bound to the same accio_id.
    
    Returns:
        On success — a Markdown confirmation plus a JSON payload with keys
        `post_id` (LinkedIn UGC Post URN) and `visibility`.
        On failure — a single-line reason plus an action suggestion. Typical
        failure categories: not authorized / scope missing / network error /
        validation error (e.g. empty text).
    
    Example:
        share_text_on_linkedin(text="Hello from Accio MCP!")
        share_text_on_linkedin(text="Launch day!", visibility="CONNECTIONS")
    meta: toolkit=linkedin, toolkit_service=consumer
      - text (string) (required)
      - visibility (string)
      - linkedin_user_id (string)

  share_article_on_linkedin
    Share an external article/web link as a LinkedIn post.
    
    WHEN TO CALL:
    - The user wants to share a URL (blog post, news article, product page,
      GitHub repo, etc.) to LinkedIn with an optional commentary;
    - The user explicitly asks to "post a link" / "share an article" on
      LinkedIn. For plain-text posts without any link, use
      `share_text_on_linkedin` instead.
    
    REQUIRED OAUTH SCOPE: `w_member_social`.
    
    Args:
        url: Required. The article / web URL to share. Must be a reachable
            http(s) URL.
        text: Optional. Commentary text shown above the link card.
        title: Optional. Title to display in the link card. If omitted,
            LinkedIn will try to scrape one from the page.
        description: Optional. Description to display in the link card.
        visibility: Optional. `"PUBLIC"` (default) or `"CONNECTIONS"`.
        linkedin_user_id: Optional. Same semantics as in
            `get_linkedin_user_info`.
    
    Returns:
        On success — a Markdown confirmation plus a JSON payload with keys
        `post_id`, `visibility`, `shared_url`.
        On failure — a single-line reason plus an action suggestion.
    
    Example:
        share_article_on_linkedin(
            url="https://openai.com/blog/xxx",
            text="Worth a read.",
            title="OpenAI Blog",
            description="Latest model release notes",
        )
    meta: toolkit=linkedin, toolkit_service=consumer
      - url (string) (required)
      - text (string)
      - title (string)
      - description (string)
      - visibility (string)
      - linkedin_user_id (string)

  share_image_on_linkedin
    Publish an image post to the currently authorized LinkedIn account.
    
    WHEN TO CALL:
    - The user asks to "post a picture / photo / image" on LinkedIn, optionally
      with commentary text;
    - The user provides a public image URL (JPEG / PNG / GIF) and wants to
      share it as a LinkedIn image post.
    - For plain-text posts without any media, use `share_text_on_linkedin`.
    - For sharing an external web page link with a preview card, use
      `share_article_on_linkedin`.
    
    REQUIRED OAUTH SCOPE: `w_member_social`.
    
    HOW IT WORKS (LinkedIn official 3-step flow):
    1. `POST /v2/assets?action=registerUpload` with recipe
       `urn:li:digitalmediaRecipe:feedshare-image` to get an `uploadUrl` and
       an `asset` URN.
    2. POST the raw image bytes to that `uploadUrl`.
    3. `POST /v2/ugcPosts` with `shareMediaCategory=IMAGE` and the asset URN
       referenced in `specificContent.com.linkedin.ugc.ShareContent.media`.
    
    Args:
        image_url: Required. A publicly reachable http(s) URL pointing to a
            JPEG / PNG / GIF image. Max 10 MB. Local file paths and file://
            URIs are rejected for security.
        text: Optional. Commentary text shown above the image.
        title: Optional. Title associated with the image in the media slot.
        description: Optional. Description associated with the image in the
            media slot.
        visibility: Optional. `"PUBLIC"` (default) or `"CONNECTIONS"`. Any
            other value falls back to `"PUBLIC"`.
        linkedin_user_id: Optional. Same semantics as in
            `get_linkedin_user_info`.
    
    Returns:
        On success — a Markdown confirmation plus a JSON payload with keys
        `post_id`, `visibility`, `asset_urn`, `image_url`.
        On failure — a single-line reason plus an action suggestion. Typical
        failures: invalid URL / oversize / unsupported format / not authorized
        / scope missing / network error.
    
    Example:
        share_image_on_linkedin(
            image_url="https://cdn.example.com/poster.png",
            text="New launch poster",
            title="Launch Poster",
        )
    meta: toolkit=linkedin, toolkit_service=consumer
      - image_url (string) (required)
      - text (string)
      - title (string)
      - description (string)
      - visibility (string)
      - linkedin_user_id (string)

  adjust_square_inventory
    Adjust inventory quantity for a catalog item variation.
    
    Creates an inventory adjustment to increase or decrease stock.
    Common use cases:
    - Receive new stock: from_state="NONE", to_state="IN_STOCK"
    - Remove damaged stock: from_state="IN_STOCK", to_state="WASTE"
    - Return to vendor: from_state="IN_STOCK", to_state="NONE"
    
    Args:
        merchant_id: The Square merchant ID (obtained after OAuth authorization).
        catalog_object_id: The ID of the catalog object (item variation) to adjust.
        location_id: The ID of the location where the adjustment occurs.
        quantity: The quantity to adjust as a string (e.g. "10", "5.5").
                  Supports up to 5 decimal places.
        from_state: The inventory state before adjustment. Common values:
                    NONE, IN_STOCK, SOLD, WASTE, ORDERED_FROM_VENDOR, etc.
                    Defaults to "NONE".
        to_state: The inventory state after adjustment. Common values:
                  NONE, IN_STOCK, SOLD, WASTE, ORDERED_FROM_VENDOR, etc.
                  Defaults to "IN_STOCK".
        occurred_at: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the adjustment occurred.
                     Must be within the last 24 hours. Defaults to current time.
        reference_id: Optional external reference ID for linking to external systems.
        idempotency_key: Unique key to prevent duplicate operations. Auto-generated if empty.
    
    Returns:
        JSON string with the adjustment result including updated inventory counts.
    meta: toolkit=square, toolkit_service=inventory
      - merchant_id (string) (required)
      - catalog_object_id (string) (required)
      - location_id (string) (required)
      - quantity (string) (required)
      - from_state (string)
      - to_state (string)
      - occurred_at (string)
      - reference_id (string)
      - idempotency_key (string)

                  Supports up to 5 decimal places.
        state: The inventory state of the counted items. Defaults to "IN_STOCK".
               Common values: IN_STOCK, ORDERED_FROM_VENDOR, etc.
        occurred_at: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the count was taken.
                     Must be within the last 24 hours. Defaults to current time.
        reference_id: Optional external reference ID for linking to external systems.
        idempotency_key: Unique key to prevent duplicate operations. Auto-generated if empty.
    
    Returns:

  js_product_database_query
    Search the Amazon product database via Jungle Scout.
    
    Use this tool to find products on Amazon matching given filters such as keywords,
    categories, price range, and revenue range. Useful for product research and niche analysis.
    
    Results are automatically deduplicated by parent ASIN (variants of the same
    product are merged) and trimmed to essential fields to reduce noise.
    
    Args:
        marketplace: Amazon marketplace code (us, uk, ca, de, fr, it, es, mx, jp, in). Default "us".
        include_keywords: Keywords that must appear in the product listing.
        exclude_keywords: Keywords to exclude from results.
        categories: Amazon categories to filter by (e.g. ["Home & Kitchen"]).
        exclude_unavailable_products: If True, exclude products that are currently unavailable.
        min_price: Minimum product price filter.
        max_price: Maximum product price filter.
        min_revenue: Minimum estimated monthly revenue filter.
        max_revenue: Maximum estimated monthly revenue filter.
        page_size: Number of results per page (default 50, max 50).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with matching products (deduplicated by parent ASIN) including title,
        parent_asin, price, image_url, revenue, sales, category, brand, rating, reviews.
    meta: toolkit=jungle_scout, toolkit_service=jungle_scout
      - marketplace (string)
      - include_keywords (string[])
      - exclude_keywords (string[])
      - categories (string[])
      - exclude_unavailable_products (boolean)
      - min_price (number)
      - max_price (number)
      - min_revenue (number)
      - max_revenue (number)
      - page_size (integer)

  start_airtable_auth
    Start Airtable OAuth 2.0 authorization flow (PKCE).
    
    Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Airtable workspace so
    that subsequent Airtable tools (list bases, read records, etc.) can operate
    on their data.  The tool returns an authorization URL — share it with the
    user to open in a browser and complete the consent screen.
    
    No parameters are required.
    
    Returns:
        A markdown message containing the Airtable authorization URL.
        The user must open the URL in a browser and grant access.
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=auth

  check_airtable_credentials
    Check whether the current user has a valid Airtable connection.
    
    This tool inspects the stored OAuth credential for the current accio_id,
    and verifies it against Airtable's whoami endpoint.  It does NOT expose
    the actual access token.
    
    Returns:
        Credential status: connected / invalid / not found.
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=auth

  disconnect_airtable
    Disconnect (remove) a linked Airtable account.
    
    If multiple Airtable accounts are connected, pass the user_id of the one
    to remove.  If only one account is connected, user_id can be omitted and
    it will be removed automatically.
    
    Args:
        user_id: Airtable user id to disconnect (optional when only one exists).
    
    Returns:
        Success or error message.
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=auth
      - user_id (string)

  list_airtable_bases
    List all Airtable bases accessible by the connected account.
    
    Call this tool when the user wants to see which Airtable bases (databases)
    are available in their workspace, or when you need a base_id to use with
    other Airtable tools.
    
    Args:
        offset: Pagination cursor returned from a previous call (optional).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with a list of bases (id, name, permissionLevel) and an optional
        offset for the next page. On error, returns an actionable error message.
    
    Example success response:
        {"bases": [{"id": "appXXX", "name": "My Base", "permissionLevel": "create"}], "offset": null}
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=bases
      - offset (string)

  get_airtable_base_schema
    Get the schema (tables, fields, views) of a specific Airtable base.
    
    Call this tool when the user wants to understand the structure of a base —
    what tables exist, what fields each table has, and the field types.
    You need a base_id which can be obtained from `list_airtable_bases`.
    
    Args:
        base_id: The Airtable base ID (starts with "app", e.g. "appABC123def").
    
    Returns:
        JSON with the list of tables, each containing fields (name, type, options)
        and views. On error, returns an actionable error message.
    
    Example success response:
        {"tables": [{"id": "tblXXX", "name": "Tasks", "fields": [...], "views": [...]}]}
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=bases
      - base_id (string) (required)

  list_airtable_records
    List records from an Airtable table with optional filtering and sorting.
    
    Call this tool when the user wants to read data from a specific table.
    You need a base_id (from `list_airtable_bases`) and a table name or ID
    (from `get_airtable_base_schema`).
    
    Args:
        base_id: The Airtable base ID (e.g. "appABC123").
        table_id_or_name: Table ID (e.g. "tblXXX") or table name (e.g. "Tasks").
        max_records: Maximum number of records to return (default 20, max 100).
        view: Optional view name or ID to filter records through.
        filter_by_formula: Optional Airtable formula to filter records.
            Example: "{Status} = 'Done'" or "AND({Priority} = 'High', {Assignee} = 'Alice')"
        sort_field: Optional field name to sort by.
        sort_direction: Sort direction — "asc" (default) or "desc".
        fields: Optional list of field names to include in the response.
            Example: ["Name", "Status", "Due Date"]
        offset: Pagination cursor from a previous response (optional).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with records array and optional offset for next page.
        Each record has id, createdTime, and fields dict.
        On error, returns an actionable error message.
    meta: toolkit=airtable, toolkit_service=records
      - base_id (string) (required)
      - table_id_or_name (string) (required)
      - max_records (integer)
      - view (string)
      - filter_by_formula (string)
      - sort_field (string)
      - sort_direction (string)
      - fields (string[])
      - offset (string)

  supplier_verification_recall
    Recall (search) supplier candidates by name/URL for a verification report.
    
    STEP 1 of 2 in the supplier verification flow. Use this tool when the user
    wants to generate a supplier verification report. Call this FIRST, then pass
    the returned company_id values to `supplier_verification_detail`.
    
    Difference from `supplier_verification_detail`:
      - This tool (recall) INPUT is a fuzzy company name or storefront URL and
        OUTPUT is a LIST of candidate suppliers (each with a company_id) for the
        user to pick from. It performs a search/match and has no report detail.
      - `supplier_verification_detail` INPUT is exact company_id(s) obtained from
        this tool and OUTPUT is the full verification report detail for them.
    
    Args:
        supplier_name: The supplier/company name or Alibaba storefront URL to look up.
                       Example: "Qingdao Etrip Smart Home Co., Ltd." or
                       "https://cnetriphome.en.alibaba.com/contactinfo.html".
                       URLs are automatically normalized to extract the company token.
        top_k: Max number of candidates to recall (default 50, range 1-100).
    
    Returns:
        JSON with payload.candidates (list of matched suppliers with company_id,
        company_name_en, company_name_cn, company_minisite_url, seller_score).
        Use company_id from candidates to call supplier_verification_detail.
    meta: toolkit=alibaba, toolkit_service=supplier-verification-report
      - supplier_name (string) — The supplier/company name or Alibaba storefront URL to look up. Example: "Qingdao Etrip Smart Home Co., Ltd." or "https://cnetriphome.en.alibaba.com/contactinfo.html". URLs are automatically normalized to extract the company token.
      - top_k (integer) — Max number of candidate suppliers to recall. Range 1-100, default 50. Example: 10.

  supplier_verification_detail
    Fetch the full supplier verification report detail by company_id list.
    
    STEP 2 of 2 in the supplier verification flow. This tool maps to RLab app
    `ICBU_P0715_314218C67`.
    
    Difference from `supplier_verification_recall`:
      - `supplier_verification_recall` INPUT is a fuzzy company name/URL and
        OUTPUT is a LIST of candidate suppliers to search/choose from.
      - This tool (detail) INPUT is exact company_id(s) returned by recall and
        OUTPUT is the detailed verification report for those specific suppliers.
    
    Args:
        comp_id_list: Supplier company_id list (e.g. ["231465246"]), obtained
                      from supplier_verification_recall candidates. A single id
                      string or JSON-encoded array string is also tolerated.
        company_id: Optional single-id alias; merged into comp_id_list.
    
    Returns:
        JSON string including filtered `payload.res` fields only.
    meta: toolkit=alibaba, toolkit_service=supplier-verification-report
      - comp_id_list (string[]) — List of supplier company_id strings to fetch detail for. Each item is a company_id obtained from supplier_verification_recall candidates. Example: ["231465246", "987654321"]. Required, non-empty. A single id string is also accepted and will be wrapped automatically.
      - company_id (string) — Alias for a single company_id, accepted for convenience. Example: "231465246". Prefer comp_id_list for multiple ids.

  set_odoo_credentials
    Set, update, or disconnect Odoo connection credentials for the current user.
    
    **When to trigger:**
    Call this tool when the user wants to connect their Odoo instance,
    or when an Odoo tool returns ``ODOO_MISSING_CREDENTIAL`` /
    ``ODOO_AUTH_FAILED`` indicating credentials are missing or expired.
    
    **How to obtain an API key:**
    1. Log into the Odoo instance with the integration user.
    2. Go to Preferences → Account Security → New API Key.
    3. Copy the generated key. Do NOT use the account password — Odoo
       disables password auth once 2FA is enabled, and API keys can be
       revoked independently.
    
    **Disconnect:**
    Pass an empty string for ``odoo_api_key`` to disconnect. The stored
    credential is removed idempotently and no Odoo API verification is
    performed.
    
    **Verification:**
    Before storing, the credential is verified against the Odoo XML-RPC
    ``common.authenticate`` endpoint. If verification fails, nothing is
    stored and a structured JSON error is returned.
    
    Args:
        odoo_url: Full Odoo URL (only *.odoo.com domains are supported), e.g. "https://yourco.odoo.com".
        odoo_db: Odoo database name, e.g. "yourco-prod".
        odoo_login: Odoo login (usually email).
        odoo_api_key: Odoo API key. Pass empty string to disconnect.
    
    Returns:
        - On success: a message containing "connected" along with the
          Odoo user name.
        - On empty key: a message containing "disconnected".
        - On failure: a structured JSON error with code and message.
    
    Example:
        set_odoo_credentials(
            odoo_url="https://yourco.odoo.com",
            odoo_db="yourco-prod",
            odoo_login="integration@yourco.com",
            odoo_api_key="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
        )
        set_odoo_credentials(odoo_url="", odoo_db="", odoo_login="", odoo_api_key="")
    meta: toolkit=odoo, toolkit_service=auth
      - odoo_url (string) (required)
      - odoo_db (string) (required)
      - odoo_login (string) (required)
      - odoo_api_key (string) (required)

  check_odoo_credentials
    Check the status of the current user's Odoo credentials.
    
    **When to trigger:**
    Call this tool when the user asks whether Odoo is connected, or
    before performing an Odoo operation to confirm auth status.
    
    This tool checks if credentials exist and re-verifies them against
    the Odoo instance. It does NOT expose the actual API key value.
    
    Returns:
        Credential status including validity, URL, database, login, and
        creation time.
    
    Example:
        check_odoo_credentials()
    meta: toolkit=odoo, toolkit_service=auth

  delete_odoo_credentials
    Delete the current user's Odoo credentials.
    
    **When to trigger:**
    Call this tool when the user wants to disconnect their Odoo account

    After deletion, the user will need to set new credentials to use
    Odoo tools again.
    
    Returns:
        Success or error message.
    
    Example:
        delete_odoo_credentials()
    meta: toolkit=odoo, toolkit_service=auth

    have a supplier reference (``partner_ref``) instead, first resolve

    then call this tool per name and aggregate at the agent level — that

        billed vs outstanding.

      - odoo_name (string) (required)
